raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From the Palais de Justice, walk on to the Conciergerie, just ahead.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"In the fifteenth century, people passing on the quay could still hear the screams of prisoners being tortured inside the Tour Bonbec, the westernmost tower.","source_id":"b2316d07-e65e-418b-98d2-a4252e3171b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"When the tower was restored in 1828, workers broke into the basement and found two oubliettes — hidden dungeons spiked with iron points and opening straight onto the river.","source_id":"b2316d07-e65e-418b-98d2-a4252e3171b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"You can guess the fate of anyone dropped in.","source_id":"b2316d07-e65e-418b-98d2-a4252e3171b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The tower's name says the rest: bon-bec is old French for prate, a nod to the interrogations on the ground floor, where torturers worked through a whole repertoire to force out confessions and denunciations.","source_id":"b2316d07-e65e-418b-98d2-a4252e3171b4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"This grim place is one of the last surviving pieces of the old medieval Palais de Justice, and it's Paris's oldest prison.","source_id":"e31a54a4-1e8b-4193-b2aa-5fdc8fab4966","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Step inside and the Gothic halls open up — the vast, vaulted Salle des Gens d'Armes, raised between 1301 and 1315.","source_id":"e31a54a4-1e8b-4193-b2aa-5fdc8fab4966","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Around 1353 a kitchen pavilion went up at the northwest corner, set slightly apart from the rest so a fire wouldn't take the whole palace with it.","source_id":"c9cf0722-12ab-4849-bbb8-295b394739a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"It ran on two floors: the royal family and their guests were fed from upstairs, the staff from below.","source_id":"c9cf0722-12ab-4849-bbb8-295b394739a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"People come here now for the French history, but those Gothic halls and the great kitchen fireplaces are worth the visit on their own.","source_id":"575ca557-acb3-419b-ba84-2917fcf07805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Both kitchens worked flat out on the sixth of January, 1378, when Charles V threw the Banquet of the Three Kings for his uncle Charles the Fourth, the Holy Roman Emperor, and his cousin Wenceslaus, King of the Romans.","source_id":"c9cf0722-12ab-4849-bbb8-295b394739a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Three courses of ten dishes each went out to the Grand Hall — to the royal guests and eight hundred German and French knights.","source_id":"c9cf0722-12ab-4849-bbb8-295b394739a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"By the Revolution the far end was walled off by an iron grille for the poorest prisoners — the pailleux, who couldn't bribe a guard for a private cell and slept on straw, the paille that gave them their name.","source_id":"e31a54a4-1e8b-4193-b2aa-5fdc8fab4966","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Beyond that ran a corridor where prisoners could wander freely, and a room they've since rebuilt — the salle de toilette, where the condemned had their hair cropped and their collars torn away for the blade.","source_id":"f3817861-6520-4bbe-8263-790afa3b11dd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The list of the doomed here is staggering.","source_id":"575ca557-acb3-419b-ba84-2917fcf07805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"There was Madame Roland, who'd backed the Revolution but threw in with the Girondins at exactly the wrong moment.","source_id":"575ca557-acb3-419b-ba84-2917fcf07805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"And Marie-Antoinette, who sat in a dreary cell from the second of August to the sixteenth of October, 1793, before she was taken to the guillotine on the Place de la Révolution — today's Place de la Concorde.","source_id":"575ca557-acb3-419b-ba84-2917fcf07805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Later came Danton, Robespierre, and Saint-Just, one after another — Danton and Robespierre in the cells right beside the Queen's.","source_id":"575ca557-acb3-419b-ba84-2917fcf07805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Upstairs they've mocked up her cell: a crucifix hanging forlornly against peeling fleur-de-lys wallpaper.","source_id":"2560212a-79e9-487c-8b0f-300b7465b06c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"North of the halls ran the stretch to the dark cells, called the rue de Paris — after the Great Executioner, Monsieur de Paris.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"That title stayed in one family, the Sansons, handed father to son through seven generations, from 1688 to 1847.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Here's the turn.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Shortly before the Revolution, Louis the Sixteenth decided to improve the executioner's lot and granted Charles-Henri Sanson an annual fee of sixteen thousand pounds, plus two thousand crowns to keep up the scaffold and pillory — never dreaming the man would one day become his own executioner.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Charles-Henri was a royalist and wanted no part of it.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"On the fifteenth of August, 1792, he was arrested as \"the despot's employee,\" and for each execution he was dispatched from his cell to the Place du Carrousel, where the guillotine then stood, and afterwards taken back.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"At first the killings were few, but once the blade was working at full swing his expert hand couldn't be spared, so they let him go.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"He retired soon after he'd executed his sovereign.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"His son Henri took over, holding the post through the Terror and every shaky regime that followed, right up to 1840, deep into the reign of Louis-Philippe.","source_id":"63007efd-b494-424c-861d-4b1671139ec9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3}]}
